resources.string: Local voice intercom for two phones
Cleaning up the previous Wi-Fi Direct connection…
Pairloom uses Wi-Fi Direct to find the other phone, and Android asks for permission to look for nearby devices. Pairloom does not use or store your location. Tap Host or Join to try again.
The permission was denied and Android will no longer ask. Open app settings and allow \"Nearby devices\" (Android 13 and newer) or \"Location\" (Android 12 and older), then try again.
Android 12 and older only allow Wi-Fi Direct discovery while Location services are on. Pairloom does not read or store your location. Turn Location on, come back here, and try again.
Wi-Fi Direct did not start or did not find a device. Some phones need Location services turned on for this even on Android 13 and newer. Turn Location on and try again.
On the other phone, tap Join and pick this one. Accept the connection prompt here if one appears.
Make sure the other phone is on Host, then tap it below.
Nothing found yet. Check that the other phone is hosting and that Wi-Fi is on, then tap Search again.
If the other phone asks whether to accept the connection, tap Accept there.
The Wi-Fi Direct group is formed. Starting the control connection.
The phones have not been paired before. Check that both phones show the same code.
Does the other phone show exactly this code?
None yet. The first connection to a phone asks you to compare a pairing code.
This phone is the Wi-Fi Direct group owner
This phone is a Wi-Fi Direct client (group owner address %1$s)
Group formed after %1$d ms, link opened %2$d ms later
Android did not report the group, so the link was opened after confirming this phone is in the other phone\'s group.
Encrypted and authenticated (%1$s). Newly paired, other phone\'s key %2$s
Encrypted and authenticated (%1$s). Paired phone, key %2$s
Round trip: last %1$s, average %2$s, min %3$s, max %4$s
%3$s · audio replaced or lost: %1$s%% · estimated delay %2$s ms plus audio hardware
Tap to talk is on while TalkBack is running
Shown while Pairloom is connected to another phone, so calls can go on in the background.
When the other phone calls while Pairloom is not on screen.
Open Pairloom to call or use push-to-talk.
The link dropped. Keep the phones close.
Tap Connect on both phones, in any order.
Tap Connect on both phones. The first time, one of them may show the list of nearby phones: pick %1$s there, and accept the prompt if one appears. After that, Connect needs nothing else.
Tap Connect on %1$s too, if you have not yet. Keep the phones close.

1. Open Pairloom on both phones and keep them close.\n2. Tap Host on one phone and Join on the other, then pick the first phone.\n3. Accept the connection prompt if one appears, and check that both phones show the same 6-digit code.
The other phone must be hosting. No connection prompt appears there. Or pick a phone from the list below.
Nothing heard from %1$s for %2$d s. The phones may be too far apart; the call ends if the link is lost.
%1$s could not start: the audio could not be opened on one of the phones.
%1$s ended: another app or a phone call took the audio.
%1$s ended: the link to the other phone was lost.
The link dropped, perhaps because the phones were too far apart. Both phones are trying to connect again for up to 90 seconds.
Pairloom needs the microphone for calls. Allow it when asked, or in app settings.
Round trip %1$s ms (min %2$s, max %3$s) · jitter %4$s ms · spread %7$s ms · buffer %5$s/%6$s ms
Rejected: auth %1$d, wrong source %2$d, replay %3$d · est. one-way %4$s ms
The other phone sent invalid data.
Wi-Fi Direct is turned off. Turn Wi-Fi on and try again.
Wi-Fi Direct is not available on this phone.
Android reported a Wi-Fi Direct error.
The other phone did not accept in time. Try again and tap Accept on the other phone.
The Wi-Fi Direct group formed, but the control connection could not be opened.
Android did not join the other phone\'s group and made this phone a separate group owner, so the two phones are in different groups. Tap Cancel on both phones and try again.
Pairloom could not confirm that the connection runs over the Wi-Fi Direct link, so it stopped for safety. Try again.
The other phone runs an incompatible version of Pairloom.
This phone\'s secure identity could not be set up, so Pairloom cannot connect safely.
The secure connection to the other phone could not be set up. Make sure both phones run the same Pairloom version and try again.

The other phone\'s identity does not match the one paired earlier. This can mean the app was reinstalled or reset on one phone, or that another device is pretending to be it. Pairloom stopped. If you trust the other phone, tap Forget for it under Paired phones on both phones, then pair again.
Pairing was cancelled because the codes were not confirmed as matching. Nothing was saved.
The pairing codes were not confirmed in time. Nothing was saved.
Pairing failed a security check. Nothing was saved. Try again.
Pairloom could not read or save its list of paired phones, so it stopped for safety.
Tap Connect on both phones, in any order.
Tap Connect on both phones. This first time, %1$s may show a list of nearby phones: pick this one there.
Open Pairloom on both phones. Choose Host on one and Join on the other.
Is this the same number as on %1$s?
Only on this phone. Leave it empty to use the name the other phone sends.
This phone waits for the other one
Find the phone that is hosting
The name the other phone sees
Clearer when a screen is off, using less Wi-Fi; about 15 ms more delay. Used when both phones have it on.
To connect to it again, you will have to pair the phones again and compare the code.
Disconnect first to forget a phone or pair a new one.
%1$s has the floor. Let go and try again.
Not heard. Let go and press again to talk.
A simulated third phone joins the group talk on this phone and beeps for 2 s every 8 s.
Lost the group. This phone keeps trying to rejoin %1$s for up to 30 minutes, and rejoins the group talk once it is back. Moving closer to the host helps.
This phone hosts the group. %1$s will be disconnected too.
The join code does not match. Check the three words with the others.
Type the three words shown on the phone that started the group.
That is not a join code. It is three words, like the example.
Read these three words to the people joining. They tap Join with a code and type them. No pairing needed.
Stay near the phone that started the group.
This can take up to half a minute. Keep the phones close.
This phone runs Android 9 or older, which cannot join a group with a code. It can still start a group for others to join, or pair with a phone.
